title: Book One · Chapter 75: A Boat That Stays Home
story:
On Friday morning, Ronan takes his wooden boat to school. He carries it in a cloth bag.

Dad wrapped a towel round it. The green end comes out first when Ronan opens the bag. The plain end catches on a fold.

“Slowly,” Miss Wu says.

He takes it out slowly. He does not pull harder. He holds it above the bag. The whole class can see it now. This is the boat from his little room.

“My dad made it.”

“Can it go in the water?” a child asks.

“I think so.”

“Has it?”

Ronan looks at the boat. He sailed it over blankets, along the shelf and across the table. He never put it in the river or school basin.

“No,” he says.

Miss Wu asks him to show the bottom. It is smooth and flat in the middle. Dad has cut the front to a soft point. The green paint ends in a line across the top.

“Why is only one end green?” Leo asks.

“We did not finish.”

Ronan expects someone to laugh. A girl near the back says her window has only one painted side too.

“May I draw the boat?” Mei asks. Ronan nods. She turns her paper sideways to leave enough space.

“May I touch it?” Leo asks.

Ronan is afraid Leo might drop the boat. But Ronan says yes quickly and holds it out to Leo.

Leo holds it in both hands. Then he passes it back carefully. He does not throw it like a toy plane. Ronan is glad. He does not say this aloud.

Miss Wu puts a small piece of waste wood beside it.

“The class will use simple pieces like this,” she says. “We can change those. We will not cut or change Ronan's boat.”

“Could we test it once?” Ronan asks.

“Your father must check the paint first. We can test the boat another day if it is suitable.”

No one will change his own boat for class. But he can still ask Dad about a test. Ronan wraps the boat again.

Mei gives him her drawing before the bell. She went over the green end with her pencil twice. Now it looks darker. There is no water under the boat.

“Why no sea?” he asks.

“It was on the desk.”

He looks at the little desk legs in Mei's picture. There was not enough space for one desk leg. It is shorter than the others. He keeps the drawing flat inside his book. Mei drew this picture of his boat. No one else drew it for him before.

At home, Dad looks at the towel before he looks at the boat.

“All dry?”

“We did not put it in.”

Ronan explains the day at school. They kept the boat dry for Dad to check. Dad runs a hand over the green end.

“It can have a short turn in clean water. Then we dry it. The paint is old, and this plain wood will get wet.”

“Can we do it now?”

Dad must return to Mr Sun in half an hour. He thinks, then asks Mum for the washing basin.

She empties it and lets Ronan fill it a little. Dad holds the boat. Ronan makes space on the floor for the basin.

The boat floats. It leans slightly towards the green end but does not fall over. Ronan gives the water one gentle push with his finger. The boat turns into the side of the basin.

“It needs a wider sea,” he says.

“This sea fits our kitchen,” Mum answers.

They dry the boat together. Dad leaves it on a dry cloth on the shelf. Ronan watches for a while. Then he puts the red sail book beside it again.
studyGuide:
## 重点表达

- wraps＝包起来
- suitable＝合适的
- waste wood＝废木料
- gentle＝轻柔的

额外情节词（不要求本章全部记住）：plain＝尚未上色的；sail＝帆；fold＝折叠处。

## 读句提示

**He does not pull harder.**

他／没有更用力拉。先看上一句：他慢慢拿出木船。

## 理解问题

1. 全班怎样对待Ronan带来的木船？
2. Dad为什么要求短时测试后把木船擦干？
